residents.name: Kraal Number Three
residents.kind: a named Pokemon in a place built for something else: a drovers' fold the herd's enemy now holds
residents.situation: On the long savanna tilt of the Arrow Creeks stands a round stone kraal twenty-two blocks across, the night fold the drovers penned their herd in when the creeks still ran. The wall stands two high and one high by turns, a gate gap on the south side between two acacia posts with lanterns on them, a stone trough, the last bale of hay, and in the middle an acacia split by lightning: one side still in leaf, the other stripped white. The drovers are gone. A Zebstrika moved in, and it does not let anything else in. The sign on the gatepost is the drovers'; the other one, stuck in the ground outside, is somebody's afterthought.
residents.story_rule: nothing here says where the drovers went: the Arrow Creeks' herds and the Drovers' Hollow (data/drovers_hollow.json) are the same trade, and this place only says that the trade left. Tier 8, gated after gym 7 like Ash (data/southern_residents.json post_fourteen).

residents.name: the Four Chimneys
residents.kind: a named Pokemon hiding among the things it looks like, and a cache: the survey was wrong
residents.situation: On the dead-flat eroded top of the plateau's south half stand four hoodoos, banded terracotta chimneys seven to twelve blocks high, each under a wide caprock of red sandstone, with a dry wash running between them. A survey cairn south of them says FOUR CHIMNEYS. Someone has stuck a second sign beside it: FIVE. ONE MOVED. There is a fifth chimney, low and round, among the four, and it is a Crustle that has carried its rock here from somewhere else. At the east foot of the tallest hoodoo a fossil-hunter's tin is set into the ground.
residents.story_rule: a joke the place tells on its own; nothing in the arc. Tier 8, gated after gym 7.

residents.name: the Glass Garden
residents.kind: a cache with a landmark: something the weather made, and somebody who came for it
residents.situation: On a dune shoulder above the south-east coast, lightning has struck the same place so often that the sand has fused: rays of glass run out through the ground from a centre, and at the end of each ray stands a spire of fused glass, the tallest five blocks high in the middle. A glass-cutter came out from the coast to harvest them and built a shade of sandstone and acacia on the north-east edge, with a grindstone to dress the pieces, a hanging lantern, and a box set into the floor. The sign over the box says what the trade was.
residents.story_rule: no character in person; the place is a trade's leftovers. Nothing gated: a cache is open to anyone who walks this far.

residents.name: the Watcher's Ring
residents.kind: a named Pokemon with a warning for a trigger, on a dune top: the law of the caravans
residents.situation: On the highest dune of the south-east, a ring of eight standing stones sixteen blocks across, cut sandstone with carved glyph-stones on their heads, four of them carrying lanterns, round a floor of smooth sandstone. The caravans that crossed the dunes to the Copperway (data/dune_ruin.json) had a law about it, and somebody wrote it on a sign outside the ring next to a broken cart. In the middle, perfectly still, sits a Sigilyph: the ring's watcher, which wakes for anyone who steps between the stones.
residents.story_rule: Sigilyph's own lore (a guardian of an ancient city) is the whole story; nothing in the arc. Tier 8, gated after gym 7. Psychic is the thinnest broadly useful type in ordinary country (docs/story/ENCOUNTERS.md), which is why the watcher is one.

residents.name: the Lady's Folly
residents.kind: a cache in a ruin, the story told by its stones alone
residents.situation: In the flower meadows of Sunset East, far from the island's one town, a ruined garden folly: a raised round floor of smooth stone ringed with eight pale columns, two of them broken and one gone where the steps were, with lanterns on two columns still standing.
